source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: Two models are given the same hard problem. Model A produces a much longer written chain-of-thought before answering. Model B produces a short visible answer but, per the addendum's description, unrolls a shared recurrent block to a greater depth internally before producing that answer. Which statement best matches the addendum?

options.text: Model B spends extra computation on a hidden representation; Model A spends it on visible text.
options.feedback: These are two different ways of buying more computation at answer time: unrolling a shared block more times, or writing out a longer reasoning trace. The addendum contrasts them without ranking one above the other.

options.text: Model A must be less capable, since a long chain-of-thought signals confusion.
options.feedback: Trace length is not offered as evidence of capability anywhere in the addendum. Writing more is simply one way to spend extra computation.

options.text: Model B is not using additional computation, since its visible answer is short.
options.feedback: This is exactly the inference the addendum warns against. The extra work happens inside the repeated pass, so a short answer says nothing about how much computation went into it.

options.text: Both models use the same mechanism, just with different output lengths.
options.feedback: Refining a latent representation and emitting more tokens are two distinct mechanisms in the addendum, not one mechanism producing different amounts of text.
